title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: recent load tests and production traces showed two issues with the continuous-batcher scheduler: 1) long-tail starvation for small low-priority requests during bursty traffic, and 2) excessive wait times when requests with similar priority pile up due to a static queueing policy. This PR introduces a set of scheduler improvements aimed at reducing starvation, improving fairness across priority classes, and adding smarter per-request timeout handling so overloaded workers can proactively signal backpressure. Changes include: dynamic priority aging (requests gain temporal priority based on wait time), adaptive sub-queue sizing to reduce head-of-line blocking, probabilistic eviction for excessively aged requests with configurable timeout heuristics, and a conservative backoff policy that surfaces early timeout metrics to the routing layer. The description below covers implementation, tests, and rollout plan. Implementation details: - Add PriorityAger which increments effective priority as requests wait; tunable parameters: aging_rate, max_age_bonus. - Replace single FIFO run queue with multi-band queue where each priority band has a dynamic target capacity and can borrow capacity from adjacent bands. - Add TimeoutPolicy that estimates expected service time using recent token throughput stats; mark requests as "timed_out" when wait+estimated_service_time exceeds request deadline, and emit a metric and debug log. - Integrate an early-retry hint so clients can be signalled to degrade to a lower-cost model variant. - Add metrics for per-band queue length, age distribution, timed_out_count, and requeues_due_to_starvation. Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve existing behavior (minimal aging, large max_age_bonus disabled). Rollout plan: feature-gate the new policies behind server flag "continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2"; rollout to Canary pool for 48h with tracing enabled, then gradually to Dedicated clusters. Checklist: - [x] core scheduler logic implemented - [x] unit tests for PriorityAger and TimeoutPolicy - [x] integration test with synthetic load demonstrating reduced starvation - [x] metrics and dashboard PR for observability - [x] included feature gate and runtime flags - [x] documented config knobs and recommended defaults Performance results: internal canary at 10% traffic observed 2.1x reduction in 95th percentile request wait time for small (<=64-token) requests under mixed-priority bursty load, and a 30% reduction in timed-out requests vs baseline. Risk and mitigations: aggressive aging can cause priority inversion for latency-sensitive high-priority requests; mitigated by tuning max_age_bonus and surgical rollout. See linked Linear items for tuning experiments.
